expectations.text: Reframes 'marketplace' — separates the stated solution from the underlying problem
expectations.evidence: Problem statement directly accepts 'marketplace' frame: 'Users cannot share or install third-party skills.' No questioning of whether marketplace is the right solution. Jumped straight to design.

expectations.text: Surfaces at least 3 explicit assumptions and challenges them
expectations.evidence: No explicit assumption surfacing. Design constraints are listed but treated as given, not questioned.
Lists 'Design Constraints' (pure bash, junction-based, cross-platform, git-native) but doesn't distinguish which are true constraints vs. conventions that could be challenged.
Only one approach presented (Git repos as skill packages with JSON registry). 'Key Design Decisions' table shows choices made but not alternatives considered.

expectations.text: Produces concrete actionable steps with success criteria
expectations.evidence: 6 phases with detailed deliverables, CLI commands, implementation details, and a verification strategy section.

expectations.text: Includes 'what we are NOT doing' or equivalent rejection reasoning
expectations.evidence: No explicit rejection section. Open Questions at end ask user to make choices but don't explain what was already rejected.
